full_judgment:
Mr. Bhishmadev Chokarabortty, J:-Since common questions of fact and law are involved in both the above cases, they have been heard simultaneously and are disposed of by this common judgment. 

 2. The above noted two rules, one in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.11214 of 2008 at the instance of accused Md. Taimur Alam Khandaker, the than Chairman of the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) and another in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.4912 of 2009 at the instance of two accused, namely, Hazi Fazlul Haque and Mokhlesur Rahman, the convener and Member Secretary respectively of Dhaka and Auto Tempo, Auto Rickshaw, Auto Truck Mailk Shramik Oikkya Parishad (in brief Oikkya Parishad) were issued on application under Section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in brief the Code) For quashing the proceeding in Special Case No.10 of 2008 arising out of Paltan Police Station Case No.48 dated 19.08.2007 corresponding to ACC GR No.145 of 2007 under Sections 409 and 109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Act 11 of 1947) now pending before the Special Judge, Court No.5, Dhaka. 

 3. Facts of the cases, in brief, are that one Md. Hanif alias Khokan, General Secretary of Dhaka Auto Rickshaw Shramik Union lodged a first information report (FIR) with paltan police station on 19.08.2007 against the petitioners and 7 others alleging, inter alia, that 37 thousand two stroke three wheeler auto rickshaws were evicted from Dhaka City in 2002 on an undertaking that the 'affected persons would be rehabilitated. In that regard an agreement between Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) and Oikkya Parishad was signed on 20.08.2002. According to the said agreement 200 four stroke three wheeler auto rickshaws were sectioned to be allotted at the first phase to the persons affected. But the accused in collusion with each other allotted only 32 auto rickshaws to the persons affected and sold out the remaining 168 by other means. The accused persons misappropriated taka 1 (one) crore in total in this way thus committed offence under Sections 406, 420, 409 and 109 of the Penal Code. 

 5. The Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka took cognizance of offence against the petitioners and another under Sections 409 and 109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and transferred the case to the Special Judge, Court No.10, Dhaka for trail. In that event the petitioner in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.11214 of 2008 moved this application from inside the jail for quashment of the proceedings whereupon and the rule was issued with an interim order of stay. This Division also granted him bail on 04.03.2009 till disposal of the Rule.. 

 6. After issuance of the Rule, other two co-accused namely Hazi Faziul Hoque and Md. Makhlesur Rahman also moved in this Court in the same forum with reference to the above criminal miscellaneous case and obtained Rule with an interim order of stay in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.4912 of 2009. 

 7. Mr. Abdullah Al Mamun, learned Advocate for the petitioner in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.11214 of 2008 submits that admittedly an agreement was signed between BRTA and Oikkya Parishad for distribution of 200 (two hundred) four stroke auto rickshaws among the affected persons at subsidized rate. Neither the petitioner nor BRTA was a signatory to that agreement. Moreover, in course of investigation the agreement, foundation of the case was also not seized by the investigating officer. If the agreement is not there with the record, the case does not stand without its foundation. The allotment as alleged was given by the Ministry of Communication and the petitioner did not play any role in it. Mr. Mamun takes us through the FIR and charge sheet' and submits that the investigating officer found that the Government was not affected in any means by the said allotment. No allegation of misappropriation of public money or of taking any financial advantage has been brought in the FIR as well as in the charge sheet against the petitioner, and as such the proceeding against him is an abuse of the process of Court. Since no offence Scheduled to the Durnity Daman Commission Ain, 2004 (Act V of 2004) has been disclosed against the petitioner, the proceeding can also not run against him. Although the charge has not yet been framed, cognizance of the offence already been taken and as such the petitioner may take resort of Section 561 A of the Code for quashing the proceeding. Mr. Mamun refers to the cases of Ali Akkas Vs. Enayet Hossain and others, 17 BLD (AD) 44; Durnity Daman Commissidn Vs. Engineer Mosharrof Hossain and others, 21 BLC (AD) 211; Abdul Quader Chowdhury and others Vs. The State, 28 DLR (AD) 38 and The State Vs. Mrs. Lailun Nahar Ekram, 27 BLD (AD) 18 and concludes that the ratio of the cases as referred to above are befitting in this case. 

 8. Mr. Nazibur Rahman, learned Deputy Attorney General on the other hand submits that the FIR and charge sheet disclose offence scheduled to Act V of 2004 against all the petitioners. The charge has not yet been framed against them and quasment of a proceeding at this stage has been disapproved by our apex Court. Mr. Rahman refers to the case of Nazrul Islam Vs. The State, 13 MLR (AD) 184 and submits that the instant petitions for quashment, before filing an application to the trial Court for discharge or waiting till framing of charge, are prematured and hence the Rules are liable to be discharged, he concludes. 

 9. The ACC being opposite party No.2 also opposes the Rule by filing a counter-affidavit controverting the facts of the petition. Syed Mamun Mahbub, learned Advocate for the ACC submits that the petitioners have challenged the proceedings of the case purely on some disputed question of facts. The charges against them are yet to be framed and there is no legal scope to entertain such application for quashment at this stage. Mr. Mamun refers the same cases of Ali Akkas Vs. Enayet Hossain and others, 2 MLR (AD) 166 = 17 BLD (AD) 44 as cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and Nazrul Islam Vs. The State, 13 MLR (AD) 184 as cited by the learned Deputy Attorney General and submits that the law has been laid down by our Apex Court in the above reported cases in respect of quashing a criminal proceeding. The principles set up in those cases do not permit to quash the proceeding of the instant case at this stage. The petitioners are to wait till disposal of an application for discharge or up to the framing of charge by the trial court. In the case in hand there is clear allegation against the petitioners of committing offence scheduled to Act V of 2004, which needs to be determined at trial upon examining the witnesses. 

 From the above quoted .part of the charge sheet which implicates the petitioner in Criminal Misc. Case No.11214 of 2008. It appears that he did not misappropriate any public money and the government was not affected anyway by the alleged sale. The charge sheet also does not disclose any offence against him of taking bribe or gratification or illegal advantage from anyone. It also does not disclose what role Taimur Alam Khandaker played in the alleged sale' for which he may be tried under any of the Section scheduled to Act V of 2004. 

 15. Although charge against him in case is yet to be farmed, but the cognizance of the offence has already been taken. We find nothing in the record to take cognizance against him. It is well settled by the Appellate Division that this Division has the inherent power to pass necessary order to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. In several pronouncements both the Divisions clearly laid down the law with regard to quashment of Criminal proceedings. Section 265C and 241A of the Code deal with discharge of an accused brought for trail. The said Sections say that when an accused is brought for trail before a Court of law, the Court upon hearing the parties and on consideration of the record of the cases and the documents may discharge the accused. They have nothing to do with quashing of a proceeding. Section 561A of the Code is an independent and inherent power of the High Court Division and this power can be exercised in case of abuse of the process of Court and for securing the ends of justice and/or to give effect to any order under the Code [reliance placed on Latifa Akter and others Vs. The State and another, 19 BLD (AD) 20]. If the petitioner Taimur Alam Khandaker waits till framing of charge or disposal of any application for his discharge or he face the trial, the result of the case against him would be the same. We find no cogent .reason to drag the case up to that stages so far it relates to him. We do not find anything on record of taking cognizance against him. The law permits this Court to quash a proceeding at this stage also to prevent abuse of the process of Court. 

 16. In 2 MLR (AD) 166 = 17 BLT (AD) 44 as referred to by the learned Advocates of both the sides, five criteria have been set up for quashment of a case by the High. Court Division, of them three are: 

 (1) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even that on the admitted fact no case can stand against the accused. 

 (4) In a case where the allegation in the First Information Report or the Complaint even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence alleged and in such cases no question of weighing and appreciating evidence arises. 

 The above quoted criteria's definitely attract the case in hand so far it relates to petitioner Taimur Alam Khandaker. 

 17. It also appears that another co-accused Barrister Nazmul Huda, the then Minister for the Ministry of Communication, named in the FIR and stands on similar footing with the accused petitioner Taimur Alam Khandaker, was not sent up in the charge sheet and eventually exonerated from the case. The charge sheet was accepted by the learned Special Judge and finally the said Minister was absolved from his liabilities. 

 18. Considering the facts and circumstances and discussions made hereinabove, we find substance in the submission of Mr. Mamun made in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.11214 of 2008. 

 19. But in the FIR and charge sheet specified allegation has been brought against Hazi Falzul Hoque and Mokhlesur  Rahman (the Convener and Member Secretary respectively of the Oikkya-Parishad) the petitioners in Criminal Miss Case No.4912 of 2009. They were parties to the agreement between BRTA and Oikkya Parishad and have supplied the list to the concerned authority for allotment of auto rickshaws to the affected persons and a meeting to that effect was held at their Motijheel office and decision was taken there from. We find that offence against them has been disclosed in the FIR and charge sheet. Since offence has been disclosed against them, it needs to be determined at trial upon taking evidence of the witnesses. We find no ground to quash the proceedings, so far it relates to them. In view of the above, we find no merit in the Rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.4912 of 2009. 

 20. In consequence thereof, the rule issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.11214 of 2008 is made absolute. The proceeding, so far it relates to the petitioner Advocate Taimur Alam Khandaker, is hereby quashed and he is discharged from his bail bond. The Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.4912 of 2009 is discharged and the order of stay passed therein stands vacated. 

 21. The Special Judge, Court No.5, Dhaka is directed to proceed with the case in accordance with law.
